body.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfying \(\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2v_b+v_a\mu_b^2+v_av_b)<\sqrt c\), \(\mathcal S(\eta,h)=\{x_{\operatorname{ATT}}\}\) and \(\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})/\sigma\xrightarrow{p}0\).
body.justification: The result certifies a nonempty positive-signal region in which fitting the extra factor is harmless at the local ATT scale.
body.gap: Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) analyze an asymptotically strong heterogeneous factor and do not contain a bounded subcritical no-absorption region.
body.consumer: It identifies the harmless side of the theoretical absorption frontier within the exact-oracle class.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(x_A=h\mu_a\mu_b=x_{\operatorname{ATT}}\).  Substituting \(x_A\) into the two-by-two profile gives
\[
\|B_{\eta,h}(x_A)\|_F^2
=\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2v_b+v_a\mu_b^2+v_av_b)<\sqrt c.             \tag{16}
\]
Therefore \(s_1(B_{\eta,h}(x_A))<c^{1/4}\).  On the entire subcritical part of the scalar line the definition of \(\psi_c\) yields
\[
\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)=\|B_{\eta,h}(x)\|_F^2-(1+\sqrt c)^2,          \tag{17}
\]
and the only term in the squared norm depending on \(x\) is \(\kappa^2(h\mu_a\mu_b-x)^2\).  Thus (17) is uniquely minimized at \(x_A\) among subcritical points.

For every supercritical \(x\), write \(s_j=s_j(B_{\eta,h}(x))\).  Since \(s_1^2>\sqrt c\),
\[
\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)
=s_2^2-(1+c)-\frac c{s_1^2}>-(1+c)-\sqrt c.                    \tag{18}
\]
On the other hand, (16)--(17) imply
\[
\Phi_{\eta,h}(x_A)<\sqrt c-(1+\sqrt c)^2
=-(1+c)-\sqrt c.                                               \tag{19}
\]
Equations (18)--(19) rule out every supercritical competitor, proving \(\mathcal S(\eta,h)=\{x_A\}\).

On a compact subset satisfying the strict inequality in (16), compactness supplies a common positive margin.  Since \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\), the corresponding finite-array inequality holds eventually, and the same calculation gives
\(\mathcal S_{NT}(h)=\{h\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}\}\).  The distance conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}profile}\) then gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
=\widehat x_F-h\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}\xrightarrow{p}0,
\]
uniformly on that compact subset.  Every division used above is justified by \(\kappa>0\), \(c>0\), and the positive supported variances in \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\).
